pistons.headline: Pistons vs. Raptors final score: Cade vs. Scottie battle goes to Raps
pistons.body:
[DETROIT, MI - NOVEMBER 20: Cade Cunningham #2 of the Detroit Pistons plays defense on Scottie Barnes #4 of the Toronto Raptors during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 20, 2026 at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, Michigan. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Chris Schwegler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

Two former teammates and two Eastern Conference teams traded body blows all night. A Cade Cunningham 3-pointer to put the Pistons up 102-101 with 20 seconds left was answered by a Scottie Barnes driving layup over two defenders to give the Raptors the lead they would not relinquish. When a Kevin Huerter three came up short as the buzzer sounded, it was decided. Raptors 105-102.

Cunningham led Detroit with 23 points and nine assists, but he was outshined on this night by his former Montverde teammate Barnes, who led all scorers with 29 points and hit his first nine shots of the night.

While it was appointment television watching the two top players on each team matched up with each other, the rest of the game was pretty much a horror show for the Pistons. Distilling why the Pistons dropped this game will sound very familiar to Pistons fans — not owning the paint.

Detroit surrendered 54 points inside to Toronto and gave up crucial offensive rebounds late. It’s one thing to see Barnes put a great game on you, but Detroit was owned inside by rookie Allen Graves making his first start of the season. He scored 20 points, had 10 rebounds, including four on the offensive end. Detroit simply had no answer for him. Certainly not John Collins.

The overmatched emergency starting center struggled again in just under 20 minutes of action. He was just 1-of-4 from the floor for three points and six rebounds. The return of Isaiah Joe from injury isn’t looking very different from when he was playing early in the season — he’s still struggling to find his shot. Joe was 1-of-6 from deep tonight. Getting those kinds of performances from your two highest-profile offseason acquisitions is not the recipe for winning basketball.

The other major issue tonight is that you were facing one of the worst-shooting offenses in the NBA and on this night, they could not miss. Some of that had to do with Detroit’s occasionally passive defense. But tonight, the Raptors players were just collectively on one. We already covered how hot Barnes was, especially early, but the sweet shooting was up and down the roster.

The rookie Graves was 6-of-9, Jakob Poeltl was 5-of-7, and Immanuel Quickly was 6-of-10. Collectively, Toronto shot 67% inside the arc tonight. Again, I’m going to point to the big black hole in the middle of Detroit’s lineup. A combination of John Collins and Paul Reed as your only big men is just not going to get it done in the NBA. The Pistons need Jalen Duren to come back desperately.

The loss to the Raptors drops the Pistons to 1-1 in NBA Cup play, but then again, I refuse to care about the NBA Cup. Detroit now goes on a mini road trip to Atlanta on Sunday and Orlando on Tuesday before enjoying seven of the next eight games at home.

The Toronto Raptors are scuffling in the first leg of the NBA season, but there is certainly a lot of talent there. Yes, Kawhi Leonard is absent with news of managing knee pain and swelling that surely puts a shiver up the spine of every Toronto fan. But they also still have Scottie Barnes, and he is delivering the young star goods as advertised. He is averaging 23.8 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 4.7 assists a night. On certain nights, he looks like the young superstar that represents his clearly attainable ceiling. On other nights, he and his team’s offense struggle and can’t seem to get unstuck from the mud. He’s doing a lot of things, but he isn’t doing it as efficiently or consistently as you’d like.

The real problems with the Raptors, though, lie elsewhere. Nobody can seemingly hit a three. RJ Barrett is getting to the line five times a game and hitting just 60% from the charity stripe. Collin Murray-Boyles has regressed, and Jakob Poeltl’s game has fallen off a cliff. It feels like if you solve Scottie, it helps you solve Barrett and Immanuel Quickley, and therefore, you solve the Raptors. Toronto has dropped six straight, and will be without the services of Barrett tonight.

Watching an Ausar Thompson and Scottie Barnes matchup could be electric. Barnes doesn’t have the defensive chops Ausar does, and Ausar doesn’t have the offensive versatility, but both could be liable to pull off a triple-double tonight. Cade Cunningham is also expected back tonight after sitting out Detroit’s win against the New Orleans Pelicans. Duncan Robinson and Ron Holland are out, and doubtful, respectively.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs Raptors preview: 2nd NBA Cup game
pistons.body:
DETROIT, MI - OCTOBER 16: Isaiah Joe #17 of the Detroit Pistons shoots the ball during the game against the Toronto Raptors on October 16, 2026 at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, Michigan. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Brian Sevald/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

Early season Fridays = NBA Cup day! The Detroit Pistons can climb to 2-0 in group play with a win over the worse-than-expected Toronto Raptors (1-1 in group play). The NBA thought this would’ve been a big game, handing out the Prime Video first game slot, but injuries, injuries, injuries.

Ron Holland, Duncan Robinson, and Jalen Duren are out again, but Cade Cunningham is expected to play. Injuries have slowed down the Raptors a ton.

RJ Barrett and Collin Murray-Boyles won’t suit up in Detroit. Kawhi Leonard remains out. His absence is the main source of Toronto’s struggle, but I still expected more.

GAME VITALS

Where: Little Caesars Arena, Detroit, MI

When: 7:30 PM ET

Watch: Prime Video

Odds: Pistons (-6.5)

The Raptors are still live even though they should be better. That said, Detroit isn’t a team that takes opponents lightly because of who’s in or out. The Pistons play the same brand of ball regardless of who’s out there on either side.

Wednesday’s 122-109 win over the New Orleans Pelicans tripled down on that point. Even a shorthanded Pistons squad without Cade manages to find a way.

Daniss Jenkins. Javonte Green. Ausar Thompson with the ball. Paul Reed with extended minutes — trustworthy things.

We got Isaiah Joe back in the lineup in that one! One of the marquee signings of Detroit’s offseason let it fly. Joe went 3-for-5 from range and put it on the floor, aiding Detroit’s flow. Bball Paul said Joe had more in his game during media day. Paul knows ball.

What do you know, it's Isaiah Joe

-Pistons able to flow into early offense with nothing there on initial push. DHO and now Joe gets a flare with an empty side
-Huerter cuts backdoor, pindown for Joe with an empty side. Turns the corner and the lob is there. pic.twitter.com/LZ8FQlRRAH
— Steve Jones (@stevejones20) November 19, 2026

The ability to leverage your shooting with live dribble decisions is an invaluable skill come playoff time. Love seeing Joe back out there, and more of that would be cool.

John Collins was on a heater (4-6 on 3s). He should get six 3s up every night with the room he has to fire. Collins will be matched up with Jakob Poeltl tonight. Poeltl is arguably the biggest hacker in the league. His 5.6 foul percentage ranks in the fourth percentile among bigs.

A lot of those Cade drives should end with trips to the charity stripe. Cade’s .37 FTr is a career high. He’s getting the calls and shooting ~86 percent at the line. That works. Cade is also putting together a strong All-Defense case, being a big-time contributor on the sixth-best defense.

Per Stathead, only Cade, Nikola Jokić, Matisse Thybulle, Scottie Barnes, and Caleb Wilson are averaging at least 0.9 blocks and 1.4 steals. Cade is doing this without fouling. He’s leveling up even more on that end.

Barnes recently declared himself the best defender in the world. I have no problem with that. He is up there. He’s a legit 1-5 defender. Anybody that good at something should feel they’re the best. That confidence got them where they are.

Barnes is Barnes, but I thought Toronto would have a more intimidating team defense. Cleaning The Glass ranks them 17th overall and 19th over the past two weeks + they are on a six-game losing streak.

The injury bug cannot be ignored, but I thought Toronto would be immune to long stretches of defensive lapses because of their suffocating gap principles.

Those principles still force turnovers at a frightening rate (2nd), but they haven’t dug in and clamped down like last year’s Raptors team. They’re still feisty enough to muddy up a game, but I expected more.

Toronto’s off-the-bounce creation takes a big blow with no Kawhi and Barrett. Barnes has more shot-making responsibilities this season. His 23.8 points per game are a career high. Immanuel Quickley will get them up. Catching fire vs. Ausar and the Pistons’ defense isn’t easy, but Toronto is looking to Quickley to provide immediate offense.

Jamison Battle is one of Toronto’s consistent snipers. He’s not a shooter you can disregard and is coming off a 19-point, 5-for-10 from 3 game. Ja’Kobe Walter can shoot it too and is quietly turning into a dependable heavy-minute wing.

With a win, Detroit could be in first or second in the East Group A division. The Orlando Magic (2-0) take on the struggling Brooklyn Nets (0-1) tonight. Should Orlando snag a win, they stay atop the group.

One game and one week at a time for Detroit in this tournament. They smacked around the Nets in their first cup game and look to do the same against the Raptors.

Projected starting lineup

Detroit Pistons (10-4): Cade Cunningham, Daniss Jenkins, Kevin Huerter, Ausar Thompson, John Collins

Toronto Raptors (5-10): Immanuel Quickley, Ja’Kobe Walter, Jamison Battle, Scottie Barnes, Jakob Poeltl

Question of the Day

The New York Knicks won the NBA Cup tourney and the real thing last year. Did that add any validity to the tournament?

pistons.body:
NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 18: Paul Reed #7 of the Detroit Pistons dunks in front of Karlo Matković #17 of the New Orleans Pelicans during the first half of a game at Smoothie King Center on November 18, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images) | Getty Images

With as long as Detroit’s injury report has been recently, it got a little longer with Cade Cunningham as a late addition tonight. After the Pistons’ big win against San Antonio last night, it’s no surprise Deuce got some rest on the second night of a back-to-back.

JB Bickerstaff, with his shorthanded roster, rolled out the unusual starting lineup of Daniss Jenkins, Kevin Huerter, Javonte Green, Ausar Thompson, and John Collins. This would’ve been a great game for Ebuka Okorie to get some minutes, but he hurt his hip with the Motor City Cruise just the other day.

This meant Detroit’s key bench pieces were Paul Reed, Chaz Lanier, and Elijah Harkless. Even Tolu Smith saw some spot minutes when Collins and Reed both needed rest. Luckily, Isaiah Joe made his return to the lineup tonight after missing the last several games. Despite having to play guys from the end of the bench and on two-way spots, Detroit didn’t struggle against New Orleans.

Remember that unusual starting lineup for Detroit? Well, every single one of them finished in double digits. Jenkins, Green, and Collins all made at least three three-pointers. Jenkins, Thompson, and Huerter all had at least four assists, though Huerter had seven and DJ added nine.

Both Lanier and Joe made three three-pointers off the bench. Reed was the key sixth man once again, though that’s not all that peculiar nowadays. Harkless played his most minutes so far this season and did a great job sharing the rock with four assists.

In a game without their star player, this was another complete team win. There’s no doubt the depth on this team is one of the best in the league, and Detroit had seven different players score in double digits. Your Detroit Pistons are now 10-4 on the year.

Be sure you didn’t miss the lob finish by Woo:

In an ultimate bit of disrespect, the Detroit Pistons are resting star Cade Cunningham tonight against the New Orleans Pelicans. The reasoning appears to be twofold — 1. Cunningham played last night. 2. The Pelicans. The poor, beleaguered Pelicans, home to former Pistons executives Joe Dumars and Troy Weaver, are not having a smooth go of it early in the season. They are 5-10, the coach is fighting with players, and a starter has already asked for a trade. That doesn’t mean there isn’t talent on the team. In fact, Dumars is being ridiculed because he’s asking for the moon and the stars from other GMs interested in some of his very useful players. That means the Pistons could very well drop a game tonight coming off the high of an absolutely gutsy performance against the San Antonio Spurs. But it also means that Detroit thinks it also has a pretty decent shot to win even without their superstar player. The good news is that while Cunningham, Jalen Duren, Duncan Robinson and Ron Holland all remain out, we might see Isaiah Joe back in a Pistons uniform.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs. Pelicans preview:  Closing out the road trip in New Orleans
pistons.body:
The Pistons have played a lot of road games so far this season.  They have also played less games than a lot of other teams because of that.  Last night’s game against the San Antonio Spurs was probably their toughest test of the season so far, and they passed it with flying colors.

The Spurs were in the midst of a 12 game winning streak and playing at home against a Pistons team down 4 players who were in their opening night rotation.  Despite that, they went into San Antonio and imposed their will and came out on top.

Now, they head to New Orleans to close out this 4-game road trip against a Pelicans team that has struggled this season.  After a game like last night, these are the exact kind of games that can be a bit of a trap, so hopefully the Pistons come out ready to play and close out this road trip with a 3-1 record.

The Pistons are still set to be short-handed, but as they proved last night, that doesn’t matter to this team.

Game Vitals

Where:  Smoothie King Center in New Orleans, LA
When:  Wednesday, November 18 at 8 pm EST
Watch:  Scripps Sports Network
Odds:  Pistons (-7.5)

Analysis

I mentioned the Pistons injuries above, as they are expected to once again be without Isaiah Joe, Duncan Robinson, Taurean Prince, Ron Holland, and Jalen Duren.  However, New Orleans is also without a slew of rotation players like Benedict Mathurin, Trey Murphy III, and Dejounte Murray.  The biggest difference is the Pistons have one of the deepest rosters in the league to overcome missing some key players while the Pelicans have a less talented roster.

None of that is to say that this game will be easy, but after a hard-fought battle against the Spurs last night, it will be nice to not have to deal with an imposing force like Victor Wembanyama again.

The Pistons depth was put to the test against the Spurs and the Pistons proved why they are one of the best teams in the Eastern Conference by coming out on top.  Of course, it was led by great 2-way performances by Cade Cunningham and Ausar Thompson, but that is to be expected of the Pistons two stars.

The Pelicans don’t present that same size-related issues the Pistons have had to deal with in their last few games, which is lucky for them.  The Pelicans do have a couple of players capable of taking over a game, like Jordan Poole and Zion Williamson, so it is important that the Pistons stay disciplined on defense, but Zion Williamson at least doesn’t tower over players like Ausar Thompson, who has had to take on more big matchups with the Pistons opting to start John Collins at center.

The Collins at center lineup has had a bit of diminishing returns lately as he has struggled to deal with size and rebounding, but it has allowed the Pistons to start Daniss Jenkins, who has been on a heater lately.  He had 25 points, 5 rebounds, and 5 assists last night against the Spurs and a couple of clutch shots.  He also had 21 and 22 points in back-to-back games against the Wizards after a 31 point game against the Lakers.  The Pistons will have a tough decision to make when Jalen Duren returns as they probably should continue to start Jenkins, but Duren doesn’t bring the same level of spacing as John Collins does and John Collins was signed to complement Jalen Duren at the four.

But, those are the good problems to have when you have a team as deep as the Pistons.

Another player to watch for the Pelicans is Jeremiah Fears, who had a triple-double in the Pelicans’ dismantling of the Golden State Warriors on Monday.  He is starting to put things together and develop into their future at point guard right at a time when Dejounte Murray has requested a trade.  Say what you want about the process in how the Pelicans have drafted and acquired picks in the last couple seasons, but they at least appear to have hit on Fears.

Another reclamation project they have hit on is former Piston, Saddiq Bey.  He earned an extension in the offseason after putting together a pretty solid season last year after recovering from the torn ACL he suffered a couple years ago.  As Pistons fans know, Bey is capable of getting hot, so he is another player they will have to look out for.

Overall, this shouldn’t be too difficult of a matchup for the Pistons, but after the emotions of a hard-fought battle last night, I would not be shocked to see a slow start out of the Pistons.  But, even with the injured players, the Pistons are the more talented team and should be able to win this game.

Lineups

Detroit Pistons (9-4):  Cade Cunningham, Daniss Jenkins, Kevin Heurter, Ausar Thompson, John Collins

New Orleans Pelicans (5-10):  Jeremiah Fears, Herb Jones, Saddiq Bey, Zion Williamson, Yves Missi

pistons.headline: Pistons vs. Spurs final score: Detroit D ends Spurs’ 12-game winning streak
pistons.body:
SAN ANTONIO, TX - NOVEMBER 17: Cade Cunningham #2 of the Detroit Pistons drives to the basket during the game against the San Antonio Spurs on November 17, 2026 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

The Detroit Pistons played their best defensive game of the year to overwhelm the San Antonio Spurs en route to a 105-93 win in San Antonio. For the Pistons, it was a true return to the identity that has defined them during the JB Bickerstaff era. Play suffocating defense, never quit on any play, and attack the paint.

Some of those qualities have been absent this year with the loss of Jalen Duren down low. Combine that with going against the hottest team in the NBA with the most dominant big man since Shaquille O’Neal, and it seemed like a recipe for trouble.

Of course, what we should have all learned by now is that the moment you count out the Detroit Pistons is the moment they deliver their best performances.

The Pistons were led by a dominant back court of Cade Cunningham, the NBA superstar, and Daniss Jenkins, the most dangerous man in the first year of a real NBA contract after cutting his teeth in the G League. Cunningham scored 27 points and added six assists. Jenkins added 25 points and five assists.

They needed to deliver big time because the Pistons’ roster was depleted even more than normal. Detroit was not only without Duren down low, but they were also without their two most dangerous 3-point threats in Duncan Robinson and Isaiah Joe, and without one of the best defenders off the bench in the NBA, Ron Holland.

That didn’t matter, because every player on the Pistons roster understood how big this game was, and that if you want to call yourself an NBA title contender, you have to bring it against a powerhouse like the Spurs.

San Antonio entered tonight averaging 118.8 points per game, and before tonight, its lowest output of the season was 104 points against the Oklahoma City Thunder. To hold this Spurs team to more than 10 points below their previous low is a statement to the rest of the NBA. The Detroit Pistons can beat anyone on any night.

And anyone can be the hero. Paul Reed hit some huge acrobatic shots down low. Ausar Thompson almost had his second triple-double of November with 14 points, 12 assists, and nine rebounds. Thompson was matched up with Wembenyama on the night so that Wemby could play a roaming free safety. Detroit counteracted that by putting the ball in Ausar’s hands and using him a lot in pick-and-roll situations. Thompson was attacking early and finding open teammates throughout the night.

The Pistons outscored the Spurs in the paint 60-44 and in fast-break points 24-15. San Antonio is the lowest-turnover team in the NBA, but the Pistons were able to ratchet up the pressure, fight through screens, deflect handoffs and entry passes, and generate 10 steals. It was a total team effort from one of the best teams in the NBA.

If ever a night felt like David vs. Goliath, this is it. Detroit Pistons fans love being the underdog, and so do many storied franchise players who have a chip on their shoulder. lions.headline: Detroit Lions vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers: Live score updates, highlights, injury news
lions.body:
DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 20: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions throws a pass during warmups prior to an NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field on October 20, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The Detroit Lions (7-2) and Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) face off on Sunday of Week 11. It’s a big game for both teams, as the Lions currently hold the top seed in the NFC North, while the Bucs are just a game out of the NFC South lead.

The Lions are rolling on a five-game winning streak, showing they can win in multiple ways. They’ve toughened up for a couple of defensive battles (19-15 over Vikings, 19-9 over Dolphins), but they can also still put up a lot of points, as they did last week in their 35-10 blowout win over the Patriots in Munich.

The Buccaneers, fresh off their bye, are also playing their best football right now. they’ve won three of their last five, and in their last game, they nearly toppled the Chicago Bears on the road in primetime. Tampa has one of the best defenses in football and a run game to match that physicality—making them a tough out every single week. Need proof? Check their losses. You won’t see a single one by more than a possession, which is why despite a 3-6 record they still have a positive point differential.

In this article, we’ll be providing live updates from Lions vs. Buccaneers, including drive-by-drive analysis, score updates, highlights, and the latest injury news for both teams. When the game kicks off at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday, simply come to this page, refresh the page occasionally, and watch as the updates pop up live from Ford Field.

First quarter

The Lions won the toss and deferred, giving the ball to Tampa to start the game. After a touchback on the kickoff, Baker Mayfield started the opening drive at his own 35-yard line. Detroit was able to produce a quick three-and-out thanks to a sack from DJ Wonnum on the opening play.

DJ Wonnum starting the game off with the sack! pic.twitter.com/l1aqtbRDs0
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026

On third down, Derrick Barnes made a nice open field tackle on a Mayfield scramble that stopped him short of the first down.

After a very nice punt, the Lions were forced to start at their own 14-yard line. But a huge play to Sam LaPorta shifted the field position immediately. Jared Goff found LaPorta up the seam for a 47-yard gain.

JG dropped in a DIME to Sam LaPorta who took it for 47! pic.twitter.com/8JnGMZ3998
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026

But two of the next three plays were Goff passes batted at the line of scrimmage, forcing the Lions to attempt a 53-yard field goal. Jake Bates pushed it wide right, though, keeping the game scoreless after one possession from both teams.

Tampa took over with great field position, and they nearly took advantage. The drive was kickstarted by a wide screen to Kenneth Gainwell for 14 yards. Then Mayfield converted a pair of third downs with a 5-yard pass to Tez Johnson, then an 8-yard receiver screen to Chris Godwin. Then Tampa faced a fourth-and-1 from the Lions’ 9-yard line, but the Lions were all over it and K.J. Britt got the tackle for loss to force the turnover on downs.

The @Lions defense is holding strong 😤

TBvsDET on FOX/FOX One
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/yy4g1meop0
— NFL (@NFL) November 22, 2026

Detroit’s offense was able to get out of their own zone with a trio of Jahmyr Gibbs runs for 10 yards, then a pass to Jameson Williams for 16, following by another grab from LaPorta for 11. That set them up near midfield at the end of the first quarter.

Second quarter

Goff went right back to Williams for another 17 yards on the first play of the next quarter, pushing Detroit near field goal range again.

Toe-tappin' Waymo! pic.twitter.com/aeoT13iBfl
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026

Gibbs then converted a third-and-1 with an outside carry for 2. Goff then quarterback sneaked to convert another third-and-1, setting the Lions up with a new set of downs in the red zone. On the next play, Goff found Amon-Ra St. Brown for a 15-yard touchdown and a 7-0 Lions lead.

The JG-ARSB connection strikes for six! pic.twitter.com/ySlgujuaVq
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026

The Bucs looked to answer with a methodical drive of their own. Mayfield converted another pair of third downs with a pass to tight end Cade Otton (8 yards) and Godwin (5). While Detroit was extremely stout against the run, Mayfield was able to dink and dunk his way down the field. But facing a third-and-13 after a delay of game, the Lions sent Chuck Clark on a blitz and he got to Mayfield for the team’s second sack of the half.

CAPTAIN CLARK WITH THE THIRD-DOWN SACK pic.twitter.com/wOm3Tn801t
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026

After a special teams penalty on the ensuing punt, Detroit was backed up at their own 14-yard line.

On the first play, Goff somehow evaded two sack attempts and found Tyler Conklin for 18 yards.

Oh my, Jared pic.twitter.com/NksGPZXREy
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026

Then Goff found Brock Wright up the seam for 27 yards into Bucs territory.

But after a false start and a pass to Gibbs that went for -3 yards, Detroit was in a hole they couldn’t dig themselves out of. At the two-minute warning, they faced a third-and-11 from the Bucs’ 38-yard line. They didn’t convert, setting up Bates for a 56-yard field goal. This time, he made it. 10-0 Lions.

With 1:48 left and three timeouts, the Bucs had an opportunity to get on the board before halftime. Mayfield scrambled for 14 yards on third-and-9 to avoid a three-and-out. An 11-yard completion to Ted Hurts and 16-yard pass to Irving moved the Bucs comfortably into field goal range. They only had time for one shot from the 23-yard line, but Mayfield connected with Hurst for the back-breaking score with just four seconds left. 10-7 Lions.

The throw 🎯 The catch 🙌

📺: #TBvsDET on FOX pic.twitter.com/nLcoZh9l03
— Tampa Bay Buccaneers (@Buccaneers) November 22, 2026

Third quarter

The Lions started with the ball looking to add to their lead. But they went three-and-out after a play-action pass on third-and-inches fell incomplete. Detroit lined up to for it, but Tate Ratledge jumped, hoping to draw the defensive offsides. Instead, he was tagged with false start and Detroit punted.

It appeared the Buccaneers had scored on an 80-yard run from Irving, but a holding call erased the play, and put the Bucs in a first-and-20 hole, instead. A third-and-17 screen came up a couple yards short, and Detroit got their three-and-out to match.

The Lions drive started out with a promising 10-yard run from Gibbs. Then Goff salvaged the drive with a 10-yard scramble on third-and-9.

Jared "Wheels" Goff pic.twitter.com/n5Umgr7oFr
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026

Two plays later, Goff, with Vita Vea in his face, hit Jameson Williams for a 57-yard score. 17-7 Lions.

WAYMOOOOOO 57-YARDER pic.twitter.com/YcSKTBYX73
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026

The Buccaneers responded with a long, sustained drive. Tampa started to get the run game going behind Irving, who had four rushes over 5 yards on the drive, including a 23-yarder to get Tampa into the red zone. Irving continued his dominant drive with a 9-yard reception, forcing a couple missed tackles along the way. Then on first-and-goal from the 1-yard line, Irving scored. 17-14 Lions.

Bucky Irving powers it through for the touchdown

TBvsDET on FOX/FOX One
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jA4eksUBiV
— NFL (@NFL) November 22, 2026

After another special teams penalty, Detroit started the next drive inside their own 13-yard line. The Lions picked up a couple of quick first downs with a 15-yard connection to Wright. Then Goff converted a third-and-inches with a QB sneak to his own 39-yard line to end the quarter.

Fourth quarter

The Lions’ drive stalled there, after Goff took a sack on second-and-5, and he couldn’t connect with St. Brown on third-and-7.

Tampa took over from their own 9-yard with a chance to take their first lead of the game. They went right back to Irving to lead them downfield. But after just one first down from Irving, the Bucs faced a third-and-12, and Mayfield’s pass was well wide of its target. Tampa was forced to punt, and Detroit took over with great field position—their own 41-yard line.

Detroit got an early extension of the drive with a well timed swing pass to Gibbs on a third-and-2 with the blitz coming. Gibbs caught it for a 10-yard gain into Bucs territory. Then the Lions got a bit of luck with a egregious facemask call on a St. Brown catch, giving them 15 extra yards into the red zone. A pair of Gibbs runs earned another first down and set the Lions up first-and-goal from the 6-yard line. It only took two Gibbs runs to find the end zone and extend Detroit’s lead to 24-14 Lions with 5:24 remaining.

Punch it in, Jah! pic.twitter.com/DZWej3yHoJ
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026

lions.headline: Best player prop bets for Tampa Bay Buccaneers vs. Detroit Lions, Week 11
lions.body:
MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Miami Dolphins during the third quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images

After a fun trip out to Germany, the Detroit Lions are ready to play in front of their home crowd at Ford Field. This week, they host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who bring a strong defensive front that will look to slow down the Lions’ high-powered offense.

Last week was a perfect week for my three wagers, and I was just a few Amon-Ra St. Brown catches away from being perfect across the board. This week will be a tough challenge with this Bucs defense, but I think I can give everyone some good options to pick from.

Here are three wagers to watch in this matchup. The odds are with FanDuel Sportsbook.

1. Under 47.5 points (-110)

This is one of the two easiest bets this week. The Lions offense can be explosive, but against a tough defense, things tend to slow down. Being at home will help, but I don’t think the Lions will drop over 30 points on Tampa Bay. Tampa has only allowed one team to do that, and it was in Week 1 against the Cincinnati Bengals. Overall, they’re averaging 19.8 points per game allowed.

This line also stays low because of the Bucs’ offense. Even though quarterback Baker Mayfield is starting, I don’t think he’ll be at 100 percent. The biggest factor overall in this offense is the run game, so if Detroit has a big enough lead, Tampa Bay can’t lean on that rushing attack to put up points.

Tampa Bay’s offense has been a step back overall, and if Detroit scores enough on this defense, it may be asking too much of their offense to answer. They’re averaging 22 points per game this season, but they’ve scored more than 20 points only four times, including a wild 43-point outburst against the Carolina Panthers. I see both offenses struggling to score many points because both defenses are playing well, and because the Bucs offense has been so poor this season. In the end, I see the point total around 38-42.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $19.09

2. Baker Mayfield under 211.5 passing yards (-113)

The second of the two easiest bets here, as I don’t see Mayfield having his way with this Lions defense. Detroit has been dominating opposing quarterbacks lately, allowing an average of 142 yards in its past three games. In comes Mayfield, who hasn’t been up to his normal standard this season, averaging 153.7 yards per game this season. Mayfield is dealing with a foot injury, so I think his mobility will be limited, which will affect his ability to extend plays.

Another factor will be the return of Lions safety Kerby Joseph. It’s unknown how much playing time Joseph will get in his 2026 debut, but he has an eye for the ball. He can make life difficult for Mayfield if his options are limited or tied up, and the Lions defense has gotten 32 sacks this season, the third most in the NFL.

Tampa Bay also leans on the running game, so Mayfield could expect running back Bucky Irving to do most of the heavy lifting.

The only way this one gets beat is if Detroit’s offense scores enough points that Tampa Bay has to eliminate the run and rely on Mayfield to pass downfield. If my prediction of a low-scoring game is correct, the run game could remain a factor and limit Mayfield’s chances to throw.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.85

3. Jahmyr Gibbs over 3.5 catches (-154)

With the Bucs’ defense playing well against the run, the Lions will likely use running back Jahmyr Gibbs effectively in the passing game. With Tampa Bay’s defense stout against the run, allowing 3.5 yards per carry and the fewest rushing yards in the NFL (712), Detroit might counter by using Gibbs as a receiver. Gibbs is coming off his best receiving game of the year (seven catches for 99 yards) and remains Detroit’s biggest weapon.

Gibbs is averaging 4.5 catches a game, and he’s had fewer than four catches only twice so far this season. Tampa Bay has struggled to keep running backs from catching the ball, allowing an average of 4.3 catches per game to running backs and holding a team below four catches only three times this year. Their last two performances were their best, allowing one catch in two games, but this Lions offense is easily the toughest one they’ve seen this season. I think Gibbs can hit this line, especially if the Lions offense keeps clicking.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $16.49

If you want to turn these three single bets into a same-game parlay, the odds are +615 and $10 -> $71.54

Record: 14-13

Brandon’s Bold Bet

If you want to go bold and build a big parlay that could pay well, put these three bets together. With how the Tampa Bay defense has been, I didn’t want to go too bold.

Jahmyr Gibbs anytime touchdown (-270)

Sam LaPorta alt receiving yards: 40 (+128)

Jameson Williams over 3.5 receptions (-132)

Speaking of Gibbs, keeping him out of the end zone will be tough work. The only team to hold Gibbs without a touchdown this season was the Green Bay Packers, and while Tampa Bay has arguably the best defense Detroit has seen this season, it won’t be enough to slow down Gibbs. Whether it’s on the ground or through the air, Gibbs will find paydirt. Tampa Bay won’t make it easy, as they have allowed the fewest rushing touchdowns in the NFL (three), but with Gibbs receiving ability, a nice Texas route could be coming his way against a Tampa Bay linebacker.

With linebacker talk, those are most likely the ones who will be matched up against Lions tight end Sam LaPorta. LaPorta has had a quiet four weeks after starting the season on a tear, but this could be a game where he returns to form. Tampa Bay is allowing 58 yards per game to tight ends, and I will set the bar a little lower for LaPorta at 40. Tampa Bay’s focus on the run game could make them susceptible to play action, and LaPorta could leak out and turn a short route into a big gain.

While Gibbs will be getting a lot of attention in Tampa Bay’s defense, the receivers could take advantage and get more opportunities to catch the ball. Wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown just came off a dominant performance in Germany, and Tampa Bay won’t want that to happen to them, opening the door for fellow receiver Jameson Williams to get more catches. Williams is averaging 3.6 catches per game, and I think he can hit at least four this week. Tampa Bay is without their top safety, Antoine Winfield Jr., which could spell trouble for them on those deep shots to Williams.

lions.headline: Tampa Bay Buccaneers vs. Detroit Lions preview: 4 key stats
lions.body:
DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 20: Sam LaPorta #87 of the Detroit Lions runs the ball during the NFL 2025 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field on October 20, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The Detroit Lions (7-2) enter Week 11 riding a five-game winning streak, their longest since early 2024. They’ll need to keep stacking wins to stay competitive with the NFC’s top teams, as several continue to add victories. This Sunday, the Lions will host the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who continue to fight for the top seed in the NFC South, a division in which every team has a losing record.

The two teams have met four times in the last three seasons, including in the 2023 Playoffs, with Detroit winning three of those games. In fact, Detroit’s only blemish came early in 2024, the game before the Lions’ previously mentioned extended winning streak.

The Buccaneers enter this matchup with Baker Mayfield trending toward starting after his availability was initially in serious doubt. Mayfield, who already missed Weeks 4-6 with a thumb injury, has also dealt with a plantar fascia injury that required time in a walking boot. Mayfield won’t be the only familiar face returning to Ford Field as a slew of former Lions now play on the Buccaneers’ defense, including Alex Anzalone, Al-Quadin Muhammad, Ifeatu Melifonwu, A’Shawn Robinson, and Miles Killebrew.

While Mayfield appears poised to suit up, his mounting injuries and inconsistent play this season leave plenty of questions surrounding the Buccaneers’ offense. Instead, this Week 11 preview will focus on the heavyweight bout between the Lions’ offense and a Buccaneers defense playing like a dominant top-10 unit for the first time since 2023. Tampa Bay enters the matchup well-rested after its bye week, while Detroit heads straight back into action after its international trip to Germany. With several familiar faces on the other side of the ball, it should be a physical, hard-hitting battle in the trenches between two units looking to impose their will.

Note: Unless otherwise indicated, all statistics are sourced from NFL Pro, FTN Fantasy, Pro Football Reference, SumerSports, or Pro Football Focus.

The Vikings’ Pirate Cousins

Having already faced the Minnesota Vikings’ defense, the Detroit Lions’ offense should feel somewhat prepared for the high-seas approach Bucs coach Todd Bowles’ defense employs: heavy blitzing and plenty of zone coverage.

With a league-leading -0.21 EPA/play and the second-best 24.9% stuff rate, the Bucs blitz on 42.0% of snaps, behind only the Vikings. That’s the third-highest blitz rate of any team over the last three seasons, behind only the 2025 and 2026 Vikings. Tampa Bay also plays zone coverage at an 81.4% rate (7th).

The Buccaneers’ defense is terrific against the run and will make it challenging for the Lions to grind it out on the ground. As much of this preview will emphasize, Detroit may need to put the game on Jared Goff’s shoulders. Staying ahead of the sticks won’t come easily, and the Lions will likely face numerous crucial third downs.

Nobody deploys more third-down zone blitzes than Todd Bowles; the Buccaneers lead the league, facing 26 third-down dropbacks while running them. Opponents are just 8-of-22 passing for 74 yards (3.36 YPA), with three sacks and one interception against Tampa Bay’s third-down zone blitzes. They excel at getting off the field. It’s even worse on third-and-long (7-plus yards), where opponents have faced 11 dropbacks and completed just 1-of-8 passes for one yard, with two sacks, 10 pressures, and zero first downs.

Overall, when running zone blitzes on third down, the Buccaneers lead the league in pressure rate (61.5%), while allowing a league-low first-down rate (15.4%) and EPA/dropback (-1.183). They’re particularly problematic at ending opponents’ drives with this tactic.

Luckily, the Lions have a slew of options to find solutions against zone blitzes this season:

Amon-Ra St. Brown: 20 targets, 17 catches, 178 receiving yards, 10 first downs

Sam LaPorta: 14 targets, 12 catches, 157 receiving yards, 6 first downs

Jameson Williams: 12 targets, 9 receptions, 112 receiving yards, 7 first downs

Jahmyr Gibbs: 10 targets, 9 receptions, 113 receiving yards, 4 first downs

That’s a good crew of problem-solving playmakers. Much of the Lions’ success on Sunday will depend on Goff’s ability to process the chaos and find his dudes, along with Juice Scruggs helping Goff sort out the protection schemes and keep the Buccaneers’ pressure packages from wreaking havoc.

An Extra Tight End to Sink the Ship

Brock Wright is one of the few remaining sixth-year players under Dan Campbell, and he had the third-longest catch of his career (29 yards) against the Buccaneers in the 2023 Divisional Round playoffs. His usage, alongside Sam LaPorta, could be a key factor in this matchup.

The Lions’ offense utilizes 12-personnel on 34.2% of plays, the third-most in the league. They rank outside the top 12 in every EPA metric (per play, dropback, and rush), as well as passing success rate, but have managed a 46.0% rushing success rate (8th) and 3.24 yards after contact per rush (3rd). With 13-personnel being all the rage this season, the Lions have leaned into it more, but they still rely heavily on 12-personnel despite its relative inefficiency. Finding solutions with LaPorta and Wright on the field might be one of the best ways to attack the Buccaneers’ defense.

The Buccaneers have the league’s best defense against 11-personnel (-0.296 EPA/play) and the second-best against 13-personnel (-0.178 EPA/play). However, when facing 12-personnel, they rank 20th in EPA/play (+0.017) and 26th in success rate (48.6%). Despite being an aggressive and physical defense, with two behemoths in the middle in defensive tackles Vita Vea and A’Shawn Robinson, along with rookie thumper Josiah Trotter at linebacker, the Buccaneers struggle when an offense goes bigger and brings that second tight end onto the field.

The Buccaneers respond to 12-personnel with their base defense on 77.5% of snaps (4th), and they’re most susceptible when matching with base personnel, which keeps rookie Keionte Scott, a favorite draft prospect among Lions fans, on the sideline. In those situations, Tampa Bay’s defense is allowing +0.116 EPA/play (28th) and a 51.4% success rate (28th). All of a sudden, they go from a top-five defense to a bottom-five defense. It’s one way to cut the fuse on the Buccaneers’ cannonball defense.

Defending the run from base against 12 personnel, the Buccaneers have faced 46 rushes. Among 28 teams that have faced at least 15 rushing plays in that scenario, they rank 19th in EPA/rush (-0.056) and 18th in rushing success rate allowed (41.3%).

The drop-off is even more dramatic against the pass. On 61 such dropbacks, among 26 teams that have faced at least 15 dropbacks in that situation, Tampa Bay is allowing +0.245 EPA/dropback (20th) and a 59.0% passing success rate (24th). Opposing offenses are also completing 69.0% of their passes (20th) and averaging 9.21 yards per pass attempt (21st). In those situations, the Buccaneers are still bringing the heat, blitzing on 55.7% of dropbacks (8th), but generating pressure on only 32.8% of dropbacks (18th) and producing a lowly 3.3% sack rate (22nd).

Add in the fact that the Buccaneers must overcome the absence of safety Antoine Winfield Jr., with Melifonwu filling in alongside Tykee Smith, leaving Tampa Bay’s defense ripe for Goff and offensive coordinator Drew Petzing to pepper through the passing game.

Baiting the Buccaneers

One way to take command of the seas and commandeer the Buccaneers’ defensive vessel is by using those extra tight ends in accordance with maritime play-action law. Against offenses utilizing 12-personnel and 13-personnel, the Buccaneers’ defense has shown some vulnerabilities, and opponents have taken notice. Tampa Bay has faced 52 play-action dropbacks with those extra tight ends on the field, the most in the NFL.

In those matchups, the Buccaneers’ defense has allowed 29-of-50 passing for a league-high 487 passing yards, 9.74 yards per pass attempt (28th), three passing touchdowns, +0.315 EPA/dropback (31st), a 51.9% passing success rate (23rd), and a 16.0% explosive passing rate (25th). They’re also struggling to force negative plays, with only a 1.9% sack rate (31st) and a 1.9% turnover rate (17th), a stark drop-off from their league-leading 5.4% turnover rate overall.

The Lions’ offensive game plan should incorporate play-action passes from those heavier personnel groupings to get the aggressive Buccaneers’ defense out of position, particularly with the overly eager Trotter, and put Anzalone in a bind while looking to find LaPorta, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, and company. It could also help neutralize Tampa Bay’s destructive turnover tendencies and mitigate some of its pass rush, including second-year breakout edge rusher David Walker (20.7% pass-rush win rate, second in the NFL behind only Aidan Hutchinson and just ahead of Myles Garrett, Chop Robinson, and Chase Young). That would give Detroit’s offensive line some relief while potentially catching the Buccaneers out of position on their blitzes.

Trips Ahoy!

One titanic strength-on-strength matchup that is particularly granular, but one I’m highly intrigued by, is when the Lions’ offense trots out 3×1 formations against the Buccaneers’ defense. A 3×1 formation features three eligible receivers lined up on one side of the offensive formation and one on the opposite side, creating opportunities to stretch and stress defensive coverage.

The Lions’ passing offense leads the league with +0.40 EPA/dropback from 3×1 formations. The Buccaneers’ pass defense also leads the league, allowing just -0.58 EPA/dropback against 3×1 formations.

On 57 dropbacks from 3×1 formations (17.1% usage rate, 21st), the Lions’ offense has unleashed an aerial assault for 904 passing yards (8.6 YPA), nine passing touchdowns, and just one interception, with a 52.4% passing success rate (2nd).

Meanwhile, the Buccaneers’ pass defense also ranks in the top five against 3×1 formations in yards per attempt, touchdown rate, success rate, and explosive play rate allowed.

However, when teams get creative with their 3×1 approaches, the Buccaneers’ pass defense becomes a shell of itself. While it’s a small sample size, Tampa Bay has faced 20 dropbacks from 3×1 formations that don’t feature the typical 11-personnel grouping, instead utilizing an extra tight end or running back (12-, 13-, 21-, or 22-personnel).

Buccaneers Pass Defense vs. 3×1 Formations With an Extra TE and/or RB:

14-of-20 passing (70.0% completion percentage, 25th)

218 passing yards (10.9 YPA, 32nd)

60.0% passing success rate (28th)

+0.068 EPA/dropback (22nd)

10.0% explosive play rate (22nd)

0.0% sack rate

I have a sneaking suspicion that come Sunday afternoon, Lions fans will see a handful of plays where Petzing uses that massive cranium of his to get creative with Gibbs, Vaki, LaPorta, and Wright on the field, splitting them out to toy with the Buccaneers’ defensive personnel and coverage principles from 3×1 looks.

lions.headline: Detroit Lions place Cade Mays on IR, re-sign CB to active roster
lions.body:
Aug 2, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions center Cade Mays (64) looks on during Detroit Lions training camp at Meijer Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

The Detroit Lions have placed prized free-agent center Cade Mays on injured reserve with an ankle injury, his second stint on IR this season. In a corresponding move, the Lions re-signed corner Nick Whiteside to the active roster and have also elevated linebacker Owen Pappoe for their Week 11 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Mays signed a three-year, $25 million contract with the Lions this offseason, but he’s had a difficult, injury-plagued first season. After breaking his wrist in training camp, Mays spent the first six weeks on injured reserve before finally returning to action in Week 7. In Week 8, Mays injured his ankle in the first half of the Lions game with the Vikings and could not return.

While initially deemed a “low ankle sprain,” Mays was only projected to miss 1-6 weeks. With that prognosis, it wasn’t surprising that he was kept on the active roster and ruled OUT for Weeks 9 and 10, as a return seemed possible in the coming weeks. However, now that he has been placed on injured reserve, he must miss the next four games (Weeks 11-14) and is not eligible to return to the active roster until Week 15 (ironically against the Vikings) at the earliest. If his ankle injury is the “high” variety, his season could already be over, but we’ll need to wait for an update from coach Dan Campbell before we know more.

With Mays now out for the foreseeable future, the Lions will continue to lean on Juice Scruggs, who has been terrific as an injury replacement. Scruggs is having a career year in Detroit and looks like a perfect fit for the system and culture. Behind Scruggs on the depth chart is Seth McLaughlin, who has only seen time this season in garbage-time/clock-killing situations and on special teams.

Whiteside was released from the active roster earlier this week when the Lions claimed EDGE Tyrus Wheat off waivers, then re-signed him to the practice squad on Wednesday. Now, three days later, he is back on the active roster, providing depth at a secondary that is getting healthier every day, as well as on special teams.

Pappoe has now been elevated for the second week in a row, after contributing on special teams in Week 10 against the Patriots. Expectations are that he will fill the same role against the Bucs.

michigan.headline: The State Of Our Open Threads - After UCLA
michigan.body:
The State Of Our Open Threads - After UCLA

When we finally won that game in the third overtime, I was glad obviously, though for some reason, I still kind of felt dead inside because has been an emotionally exhausting season for many, many reasons. That said, it was nice to actually be the spoiler, and despite me asking, as the second overtime began, "Why does this need to be this hard?", I actually did have a slight smirk at the end, or so my wife told me.
You will be interested to know that this was the smallest thread of the year to date, and because next week is OSU, it will likely be the smallest thread this season. There were only 2,118 posts when the two-point conversion succeeded and Michigan won, and in those posts, only 875 total instances of tracked words, which translates to an efficiency of 2.42. Historically, that's the territory of a comfortable win, although the bulk of those comfortable wins came under Harbaugh when we look at the totality of the data through time, and of course, this particular win was anything but comfortable.
In any case, the trend is below. As with many things, the emotional climax was MSU, and it has been downward since then.

"Fucks" were actually nearly steady this week - we gave 159 fucks in the thread, which is only slightly up from 156 during the much more lopsided Oregon game. We also gave a season low of 46 shits.

You can see an even more dramatic calming trend here. There were only 50 instances of "fire" this week, down from 133 during the Oregon game, which was in turn down from 291 during the MSU game. The season average is 99 instances, which is insane really since it never was even close to that during Moore's two years and certainly not under Jim and not even under Hoke.
"Suck" has been more stable. There were 41 mentions of "suck" this week, which is actually ever  so slightly up from 37 during the Oregon game.
You can also see the comparison of mentions of "Whittingham" and "fire" being right on track with one another, more or less. We are consistent and unified in the message, if nothing else.

Of course, certain things continue to be dreadful. Here is something we have been tracking all year, and yet again, "suck" and "offense" do seem to appear together a lot, and you know why as well as I do - because the offense sucks.

The mentions of the "defense" ticked upward, and much of it was complimentary. All year, the defense has done its job for the most part, and we have remarked on how much a top-tier defense is being wasted when paired with an offense that could not find the endzone with a map during most games, although they did find it once last night, and then once again in OT when it mattered, although it was a conversion play. That gets into mentions of the "offense" being down, and as you will note, being on a mostly downward trend since the Minnesota game. It is what it is. That might have been when we honestly threw our hands up about it.

It's all over the place, the normalized chart, but you get it - "fire" (yellow) climaxed during the MSU game, "fuck (light blue) during the Indiana game, and "shit" (orange) and suck" (dark blue) during the Minnesota game. That's basically the season in summary.

And now, we get to play the worst OSU team in 15 years. Who the hell knows what happens now?

michigan.headline: Michigan, Kyle Whittingham ready for ‘hostile’ Ohio State environment
michigan.body:
COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 14: The Ohio State Marching Band performs prior to a game between the Ohio State Buckeyes and the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The clock hit zero, overtime was played, and fans rushed the field (again) in Ann Arbor on Saturday, with Michigan landing a knockout punch to end No. 4 UCLA’s perfect season. A win like that is worth celebrating, but as we all know, the attention quickly shifts at this point in the year with it officially being Ohio State week.

For many in the Michigan fan base and inside the program, this has been a season to forget, with the Wolverines now standing at 6-5 overall. To the south, it’s also been a season that hasn’t gone as planned, with Ohio State losing on Saturday to drop to 7-4 on the season.

This year’s rendition of The Game is shaping up to be a matchup between the easily stoppable force and the very moveable object. But make no mistake, these sides still don’t like each other at all.

Michigan finds itself needing to get back in the win column against the Buckeyes, and it’ll be doing so with first-year head coach Kyle Whittingham who, despite the big win on Saturday, still has plenty of questions about his job security.

Whittingham, of course, has never coached against Ohio State as Michigan’s head coach, but he has coached against Ryan Day before. His Utah team lost to the Buckeyes in the Rose Bowl, 48-45, on New Year’s Day of 2022. Coaching in the maize and blue in The Horseshoe is a different beast, but it’s something Whittingham believes he’s ready to take on.

“I can envision it,” Whittingham said after the UCLA game. “I’ve never been in The Shoe, I’ve never played in that stadium. We (Utah) did play Ohio State in the Rose Bowl, so we’ve had a taste of that. We know they’re a very good football team, very talented.

“I think the environment I’m anticipating to be very hostile, but I’ve been in hostile environments before, so I don’t know if it’s going to blow all those away or not, but we’ll find out.”

Despite Ohio State being in the midst of a down season, the Buckeyes will still enter Saturday’s matchup as the heavy betting favorite, with their home crowd being part of the equation. Regardless of the record, Ohio Stadium has long been one of the most hostile environments in the country and always turns it up a notch when Michigan comes to town.

Whittingham will be going for an elusive feat when he takes his team to Columbus, as he’ll look to be the 10th Michigan head coach to beat the Buckeyes in their first matchup and just the fifth to do so on the road, with Sherrone Moore being the last to do so in 2024.

While going for the win, Whittingham will be doing so against the backdrop of comments he made in the summer about the Buckeyes, ruffling the feathers of Michigan fans when he said the rivalry could be “intense and emotional without the hatred factor.” Furthermore, he’ll likely be coaching for his job with Michigan’s new athletic director, Trev Alberts, who is set to make a decision on the program’s future in the coming weeks.

Even if this year’s edition of The Game has a different feel, the disdain between both teams should still be there in spades, and it’s something Whittingham and his band of assistant coaches will get to experience for the first time. They’ll have no choice but to be prepared for it, with plenty riding on the line for them.

michigan.headline: Michigan Football somehow drops in ESPN SP+ after upsetting No. 4 UCLA
michigan.body:
ANN ARBOR, MI - NOVEMBER 21: Bryce Underwood (19) of the Michigan Wolverines looks to pass while under pressure from Anthony Sacca (39) of the UCLA Bruins during a college football game on November 21, 2026 at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images

Michigan overcame the odds on Saturday and secured the biggest win of its season, defeating previously undefeated UCLA by an 18-16 final score in triple overtime at The Big House.

And believe it or not, Michigan actually dropped in ESPN and Bill Connelly’s SP+ rankings, going from No. 43 to No. 44 after the big win.

For those of you who might be new to SP+, it’s an advanced metric that takes into account a team’s offensive, defensive, and special teams efficiencies. It combines all three metrics into one uniform metric that predicts how many points a given team would defeat (or lose to) the “average” college football team by on a neutral field.

In other words, it’s a metric designed to look at how “good” teams really are at different aspects of the game rather than ranking them purely on their resumes. In Michigan’s case, it now has a rating of 6.6 after the win over UCLA, meaning it’d be projected to defeat the “average” college football team by about a touchdown on a neutral field.

The Wolverines blew up the SP+ projection with their win over the Bruins, pulling off the win despite entering the week as about a two-touchdown underdog according to the ratings. The win pushes Michigan to 6-5 on the year, making the team bowl-eligible.

There’s still one more game left to play, though, and that’s The Game at Ohio State. It’s been a bad season for Michigan, but it’s been disappointing for their neighbors to the south as well. The Buckeyes now sit at 7-4 on the season after losing at Nebraska.

This will be the first time since 2011 that Ohio State enters The Game with four losses, and it’ll be the first time since 1966 that both Michigan and Ohio State both have at least four losses heading into the matchup.

Despite both teams limping to the finish line, the Buckeyes will still come into the contest as a big favorite according to SP+. The Buckeyes are ranked as the No. 8 team in the country with a rating of 22.9, meaning they’re projected to beat Michigan by about 16 points.

We’ll see if Michigan has one more upset in it to close out what’s been an otherwise disappointing year.

michigan.headline: Kyle Whittingham calls Michigan’s OT victory over UCLA a ‘signature win’
michigan.body:
ANN ARBOR, MI - NOVEMBER 21: Head coach Kyle Whittingham of the Michigan Wolverines looks on during a college football game against the UCLA Bruins on November 21, 2026 at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images

On Saturday afternoon, everything that could have gone right for Michigan did.

The Wolverines got a signature win against No. 4 UCLA that might just save head coach Kyle Whittingham his job. To do so, Michigan excelled in areas it has all season, while making a few crucial adjustments to come away with a marquee win instead of yet another disappointing loss.

“Every game’s important, I know we lost some nail-biters earlier in the season, disappointing losses,” Whittingham said postgame. “Certainly I guess you could say it’s somewhat of a signature win for our program, at least this season. … They’re a complete football team. UCLA is very deserving of their ranking, and so that makes it all that much sweeter when you’re able to get the victory.”

Michigan has been on the losing side of some incredibly disappointing losses — whether it be because of the caliber of opponent or fashion in which the Wolverines lost. But in every game, aside from last week’s loss to Oregon, the defense has held the fort down, win or loss. And they showed up to stymie the Bruins, especially in the run game by allowing just 107 yards on the ground.

When looking at Michigan’s less favorable outcomes, losses to Minnesota and Michigan State seem almost entirely inexcusable. But losses to No. 15 Iowa and No. 8 Indiana could have easily ended the same way that Saturday did against UCLA.

A last-second touchdown for the Hawkeyes and the overtime win for the Hoosiers are what separate Michigan from having three ranked conference wins instead of just one.

“The two that come to mind, Iowa and Indiana, really should have won both of those games — and we didn’t,” Whittingham said. “We’ve had a lot of close games, and I think we probably lead the nation in one score games determining the outcome.”

The point that’s been harped by Whittingham all season long has been the turnover margin. Coming into Saturday’s game, the Bruins had not lost the turnover margin in a game and were leading the Big Ten with a +16 margin.

Whittingham attributes Saturday’s win largely due to winning the turnover battle by only turning the ball over once and generating three takeaways defensively.

“Got three takeaways, and that’s probably the biggest deal,” Whittingham said. “If you say, ‘What did the defense do this week that was the biggest contributor to the win?’ was +2 in the turnover margin because they were able to get three takeaways.”

Two additional key improvements from previous weeks were penalties and field goals. What seemed like a major penalty issue at the beginning of the season, often extending drives for the opponent or putting Michigan behind the sticks, felt like it didn’t matter at all against the Bruins.

Additionally, making a midseason kicking change from Trey Butkowski to Jacob Baggett is proving to be the right choice, at least in this game. Michigan went from 5-for-11 on field goals going into the game to having Baggett nail three field goals — including two in overtime periods from 29 yards out and 52 yards out.

“Proud of Jacob, it’s no secret that we’ve struggled with field goals this year,” Whittingham said. “Just to hit all three of his kicks and those last two were extreme pressure situations. Very proud of him and his ability to keep us in the game, because that’s essentially exactly what he did.”

Michigan still has its most important bout ahead of it. Heading down to Columbus next week is still going to be Whittingham’s most important game of the season. But for the time being, he can relish in the fact that his team finally came away with a signature win over the No. 4 team in the country.

“First of all, I’m so thrilled for the seniors, the guys that played their last game in the big house, that was the point of emphasis all week long is to send those guys out the right way,” Whittingham said. “So proud of those guys. Love this football team.”

michigan.headline: Unlikely heroes in TE room fire Michigan Football to upset win bs UCLA
michigan.body:
I don’t believe it. You probably don’t either. But it’s happened.

The unranked Michigan football team, mired in a season shaped by disappointment and mockery, has beaten an undefeated, top-five team in the country. The Wolverines stunned No. 4 UCLA, 18-16 in triple overtime. And they did it off the backs of a position group that hasn’t been at its best all year long.

Michigan has lacked a tight end capable of shouldering the offense this season for the first time in years. Following the steady play of Marlin Klein and Colston Loveland, the Wolverines rolled out a more ragtag array in 2026, led by Hogan Hansen and Jalen Hoffman. But that group stepped up on Saturday, delivering both of Michigan’s scoring plays in its most stunning victory of the year.

“I’ll tell you what, Mason Bonner did some good things tonight as well, and he’s a tight end technically,” head coach Kyle Whittingham said. “He’s played mostly, flexed out in wide receiver … but those guys have been great contributors. Hogan Hansen’s contributed throughout the season as well…”

After three relatively tepid quarters, it was Bonner who broke open the scoring. With a clean pocket, Underwood was able to find Bonner right into the end zone to his left, who made a hugely impressive one-handed grab for the score. It was the freshman’s first receiving touchdown of his career, and though a boom-or-bust outing — three grabs for 47 yards and the touchdown — he certainly made a mark.

The other tight end to make a mark didn’t actually record a single reception on the stats sheet. Yet his play was the game-winner. With the game into triple overtime and Michigan needing a successful two-point conversion to win, Hoffman, a former walk-on and senior who had recorded zero receptions in his first three seasons, practically ripped the ball out of the defensive back’s hands for the win — a Hollywood moment.

“I’m just proud of that room,” Hoffman said. “And we’ve all went through a lot, virtually the whole team’s went through a lot. We kept working, kept fighting, and when opportunities came, we made plays.”

All year long, the Wolverines’ tight ends room hasn’t been the crux of the offense. The position group’s statistical leader is Hansen with just 128 yards. Even in a highly dysfunctional year of offense for Michigan, the burden has been shouldered by the receiving room, as injured wideout JJ Buchanan has captured the lions’ share of yards and targets.

But that didn’t matter on Saturday — because when Michigan needed help, it got it from two unlikely heroes.

msu.headline: El Niño hits Spartans in The Weather Report
msu.body:
EAST LANSING, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 20: Dylan Raiola #8 of the Oregon Ducks celebrates his teammates second half touchdown run against the Michigan State Spartans at Spartan Stadium on November 20, 2026 in East Lansing, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images

Lots going on in the world of MSU sports this weekend. So, we thought let’s have some weather report fun and incorporate basketball, hockey and football all into this week’s report. Football was an ugly blood bath that we all saw coming. Hockey pulls off a split but had its own blood bath brawl in Yost. Basketball saw some solid bench action but the post is not looking good with the center position. Fellow TOC writer O helped out with this report and the basketball sun and cloud are coming from him. Without further adieu let us step into some sunshine.

Sun #1

My first sun is for the Spartan football team and coaches. They lost 45-7 you say, how could you possibly award the team a sun? This team has looked bad, and have had some very ugly games. This team has also had injuries that have superceded the last two years and those years were bad. What has changed this year is character. The team has character and fight. They are giving their best and not giving up. The number of underclassmen getting playing time, the number of athletes that are not the four stars Oregon is sending out there are all getting strong character development in Spartan grit. Fitz has the team playing. I’d be interested to see if he can get better athletes and take a good look at conditioning and what is going on with all these injuries. I know there is one more game but next year will really be the year to see what Fitz can actually potentially do.

Sun #2

Sun two brings us to the ice. MSU hockey has been off to a tough start and has been disappointing. Struggling to find their chemistry and identity with all the youth and lacking a true leader. Well, this weekend against the weasels MSU had an opportunity to perhaps turn the season in the right direction. Friday was an ugly game where the Spartans were manhandled and it all started with an early power play that had MSU behind practically from the start. Then we get to the melee. The hip check that the weasels felt very offended by. Barnhill and Vansaghi may have fought life back into this team. Even with both players suspended for game two and into the OSU series, they maybe let out frustrations of an entire team in an early season. Saturday night, an entirely different MSU team took the ice. Down defenders, Ward and Jurecki brought energy and the sticks were active Saturday. MSU out shot, out played, and out scored the number one team in the country. They looked like the team we have been waiting for. Yes, the weasels were short forwards, but MSU was down defenders. Ravensbergen looked outstanding, except when he left his post open, but still had the shut out. This might be a breath of fresh air that they needed to get into the winning column. The team is talented, now let’s continue to play like it.

Sun #3

Our basketball sun is going to Kur Teng. Teng had a career high 24 points on 8/11, and 5/8 from 3. Teng showed he can be a reliable shooter for this team. This allows the team to not rely on Scott and Jervis and sometimes Fears for all the perimeter shooting. Teng has always been smooth from three but has never been consistent or had a break out performance. Hopefully Teng can get hot and be a weapon that draws coverage which can perhaps open up some paint play if the MSU big men can handle it.

Cloud #1

Football cloud goes to the teams health. MSU was doubled in yardage, had two turnovers, were terrible on third down and I’m still giving the cloud to health. The injuries on this team need to be figured out. Injuries have haunted this team for a few years now. So, what’s going on? Is there something going on in conditioning or practices? Is it dietary? Is it really just bad luck? Conditioning coaches have changed and we still have the problem. This year though, was unbearable. The injuries were so much it had to be difficult to game plan when you don’t end up having the players you need on the field. It is nearly impossible to be competitive against an Oregon with third string players and a freshman QB.

Cloud #2

As much as the brawl helped inspire my hockey sun, that same brawl inspires my hockey cloud. Losing Barnhill and Vansaghi for one game is bad enough. The reprucussions of suspensions could be greater and have implications down the road. Having a significant penalty means the two are going to have to stay out of trouble or a worse suspension will come their way. That is a tough ask for a player like Vansaghi who is the agitator  for MSU. He is the guy that comes to the defense of his teammates and will throw a punch at anyone. To have him have to change his way of play could be a learning process. In a team that needs a bit more leadership, Vansaghi is a guy that can provide that, the chip on the shoulder, and the aggression. MSU needs him, so the suspensions will be something to keep an eye on.

Cloud #3

Our basketball cloud has been hinted at some but we can officially say it now goes to the centers. Taylor, McCulloch and Bonke had three combined field goals. They had six turnovers. None of them can be relied upon to be fed the ball in the low post and make a move to beat a defender. They are only scoring on rebounded put backs or a wide open Fears feed. To make things worse, the coaching staff didn’t even try to run any of those sort of plays. Bonke has been disappointing all season and Taylor is still developing. Regardless, the Spartans need a lot more production from the big guys in the paint. MSU typically struggles at the arc but has had some success there this season. If they can get stronger in the block and stay hot outside, they will be very difficult to beat. Hopefully, they can work out these kinks before the schedule gets even tougher in B1G play.

There we have it. As a big follower and fan of MSU hockey, I was very happy to see this team look like itself and take down number 1 at Munn. That was my favorite moment of the weekend. The lineup changes may be the key to staying hot on the ice. As always, I look forward to seeing where your clouds and suns lie in the comments. I wish you all a Happy Thanksgiving and be thankful there’s only Rutgers left on the football schedule. Go Green!

msu.headline: Instant Recap: Michigan State gets stomped by Oregon
msu.body:
Michigan State’s Derrick Simmons, left, tackles Oregon’s Da'Jaun Riggs during the first quarter on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026 in East Lansing. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co

Whew, boy. That was the worst loss of the season.

It was all Oregon tonight. Michigan State’s offense struggled early, and Oregon scored halfway through the first quarter to give the Ducks a 7-0 lead behind a Brandon Smith 5-yard touchdown run.

Frederick Moore had a nice one-handed snag right before the second quarter started, but Liam Boyd would miss a 47-yard field goal for Michigan State’s first chance to put points on the board. The offense was starting to look solid behind Kayd Coffman’s play, but he would trip while running out of the pocket to turn the ball over on a 4th-and-3 from Oregon’s 28-yard line.

The defense did their best to keep the Spartans close, but their special teams did not. Chrishon McCray would muff the next punt by the Ducks to allow Oregon to take over in the redzone. The defense held tough and forced them to kick a field goal, and it made it a 10-0 game. Near the end of the first half, Dan Lanning called a fake field goal where the Ducks’ kicker was able to run it in from 15 yards out to give Oregon a 17-0 lead heading into halftime.

Once that fake field goal scored, it felt like the game was already out of reach.

Oregon opened up the second half with another touchdown run, this time from Simeon Price, to put them up 24-0.  Michigan State would respond with a touchdown of their own with a direct snap from the 1-yard line by Jaz Patterson, though it would be the only points they scored all night.

Both Brandon Smith and Simeon Price would add another touchdown run each for the Ducks, and Dylan Raiola found Dakorien Moore for a nice one-handed touchdown pass as Oregon continued to pile on the points. Oregon would go on to win 45 to 7. Michigan State moves to 3-8

Kayd Coffman completed 10 of his 19 passes for 106 yards and one interception. Jaz Patterson handled 16 carries, but only managed 26 yards. Brandon Tullis added 25 yards on eight carries. The Spartans’ leading receiver was Fredrick Moore with 31 yards on two catches.

It was a brutal loss, and one of those games where you wish it could’ve ended by the end of the third quarter, as Oregon kept putting more and more points on the scoreboard. Luckily for the Spartans, it’s not the end of the season, and they’ll finish it off with a matchup at Rutgers on Thanksgiving weekend. Let’s hope they can finish the season with a win.

Go Green!
